meta.title: Aharon Sitbon – Chassidic Singer & Composer, Jerusalem | אהרון סיטבון
meta.description: Official site of Aharon Sitbon, Chassidic singer and composer in Jerusalem, once Gilbert Sitbon of the French stage. Listen to the albums Shehecheyanu and Higia Zman Geulatchem, Adon Olam and his music videos, and book a concert.

hero.title: The voice that returned after 30 years of silence

manifesto.eyebrow: From the Olympia to the walls of Jerusalem
manifesto.text: He once sang about love in French, under the name Gilbert. Then he fell silent for thirty years to study. Today the same voice sings in Hebrew, for joy and for faith.

items.title: The story
items.text: Gilbert, Gilles d'Avray, Gilbert Sainroch, then Aharon: a life no one would have dared to script.

items.title: The music
items.text: Two albums and more than twenty singles since 2014, all here, song by song.

items.title: On stage
items.text: Concerts, weddings, farbrengens, community evenings and Zoom concerts, in Israel and in France.

span.title: Fifty years, one voice
span.text: In 1977 he appears on French television and sings at the Olympia. Nearly fifty years later he sings before the walls of the Old City. In between: thirty years of silence, and a promise kept.

story.title: From Gilbert to Aharon
story.intro: The great turning points of a life in two acts, as the press has told them. The rest he tells best himself, on stage.

steps.title: A house full of music
steps.text: He grows up in a traditional family of nine children. His older sister sings and plays the oud; one of his brothers will become a drummer for the great names of French song.

steps.title: The guitar
steps.text: The family settles in France, first in Marseille, then Paris. At around seventeen, the guitar takes hold of him for good.

steps.title: The stage
steps.text: A contest won, a first single, tours. He is known as Gilles d'Avray, Gilbert Sainroch or Gilbert Sitbon. His manager, Roland Bismuth, also looks after Yves Duteil and Michel Fugain.

steps.title: The Olympia
steps.text: He appears on Philippe Bouvard's TV show and sings six songs at the Olympia, opening for Herbert Pagani.

steps.title: Tefillin
steps.text: In Paris, Chabad Chassidim offer him to put on tefillin. It shakes him deeply. Little by little he leaves the stage, just as he is offered a long touring contract.

steps.title: Silence
steps.text: He studies Torah and earns his living in other ways. His children, then his grandchildren, have no idea he was ever a singer.

steps.title: The old guitar
steps.text: Settled in Israel, in Jerusalem, he takes out his old guitar. A melody by his friend Michel Fugain keeps him awake at night, and he sets the words of Adon Olam to it.

steps.title: Adon Olam
steps.text: Producer Yuval Stoppel hears it and releases it as a single. Unsure about a comeback at his age, he opens the Lubavitcher Rebbe's letters and reads that an artist who returns to faith should place his talent in the service of holiness. He has his answer.

steps.title: Two albums
steps.text: “Shehecheyanu”, whose proceeds went to the Eshel Tsion charity, then “Higia Zman Geulatchem”, three years in the making with Eli Klein and Yitzy Berry.

steps.title: More songs
steps.text: “Or Be'einai”, a melody he was already singing in 1977, “Odeh Hashem Elokai” during the war, “Tefila LeShalom”, then “Niggun Yehudi” for Purim. His mission: to bring joy to the Jewish people.

french.title: Before Aharon, there was Gilbert
french.text: In the 1970s he records singles, tours France and is played on the radio. He had stopped listening to those records himself. Here they are, together.
french.lahayeText: One of his songs, covered by Jean-Luc Lahaye on the album “Gloria” in 1984.
french.tvText: A rare archive: the young Gilbert Sitbon, microphone in hand, in a Paris television studio.

family.title: Singing with his own
family.text: On stage and in the studio, the music is handed down. He often sings with his son, the Chassidic singer David Sitbon, and sometimes with his grandchildren.
